title: When the Burgers Outsold the Ice Cream: Jollibee's Change of Course
dek: A family that opened two Magnolia ice-cream parlours in Manila in 1975 followed its customers to hamburgers, and in 1978 gave up the franchise to become Jollibee.

story.event: Turning two franchised ice-cream parlours into a fast-food chain of the family's own
story.summary: In 1975 Tony Tan Caktiong, then 22, opened two Magnolia ice-cream parlours in Metro Manila with family savings and relatives. Customers asked for hot food, hamburgers began to outsell the ice cream, and in 1978 the family cancelled the Magnolia franchise and converted the parlours into fast-food outlets under its own brand, Jollibee. When McDonald's entered the Philippines in 1981, friends urged them to sell or close; they stayed, and Jollibee became the country's largest fast-food chain.
paragraphs: In 1975 Tony Tan Caktiong, a 22-year-old who had studied chemical engineering, opened two small ice-cream parlours in Metro Manila under a franchise from Magnolia Dairy, one of them in Cubao. The money was family savings, and the work was a family affair: his brother Ernesto later named Tony, his wife Grace, their siblings and a brother-in-law as the people who set the shops up. They knew restaurants; their father had run a Chinese restaurant in Davao, where Tony had washed dishes and cleared tables.

The parlours drew customers by giving more than expected, Tony later said: bigger scoops and cleaner shops. But people kept asking for something hot. The family added sandwiches and hamburgers, and the burgers began to outsell the ice cream. Ernesto remembered one small trick: they put the grill at the front and set the exhaust hood so that the smell of beef blew out towards the street.

By 1978 the shops had become something other than ice-cream parlours. The family cancelled the Magnolia franchise and turned them into fast-food outlets under a name of their own. They chose a smiling red bee, Tony said, because bees stand for hard work and honey for the sweet things in life, with "jolly" for happiness. He later called the early mascot "a rather crude, strange-looking bee that no bank dared to touch."

A harder test came soon. When McDonald's entered the Philippines in 1981, many friends advised the family to sell or close. Tony recalled having five stores then; Ernesto, in a later speech, said twelve. They stayed, trusting, as Ernesto put it, that their food tasted better. Tony said he had taken an outlook from his mother: "Our role is to do what we can as best we can and don't worry about the outcome." It let him, he said, sleep well at night.
Jollibee listed on the Philippine Stock Exchange in 1993 and became the country's largest fast-food chain, ahead of McDonald's at home.

quote.text: not become over fond of the lot which fate has assigned to us, but transfer ourselves to whatever other condition chance may lead us to, and fear no alteration, either in our purposes or our position in life, provided that we do not become subject to caprice
quote.work: Of Peace of Mind (De Tranquillitate Animi), in the Minor Dialogues
quote.locator: Dialogues, Book IX, "Of Peace of Mind", chapter XIV
quote.source_title: Minor Dialogues, Together With the Dialogue on Clemency, tr. Aubrey Stewart, Project Gutenberg eBook #64576
quote.connection: Seneca advises holding plans loosely enough to move where circumstances lead, but not so loosely that we chase every whim. The Tan Caktiongs let go of the ice-cream franchise they had chosen, and the change followed what customers asked for again and again, not a passing fancy.

reflection: It can feel like disloyalty to drop the thing you set out to do. The family had chosen ice cream; their customers chose burgers. What the family did well was notice which was happening, rather than defend the original plan.

Tony Tan Caktiong's mother's rule is worth keeping close as well: do what you can as well as you can, and leave the outcome. He credited it with letting him sleep. Some of what you are carrying today is outcome rather than work, and the outcome is the part you can put down tonight.
invitation: Before you finish today, split your list into what you can still do and what is only waiting on an outcome. Do one thing from the first half, and leave the second half until tomorrow.

cross_checks.claim: Aged 22 and using family savings, Tony Tan Caktiong opened two Magnolia ice-cream parlours in 1975
Customers asked for hot food, and hamburgers came to outsell the ice cream
In 1978 the family dropped the Magnolia franchise and converted the parlours into fast-food outlets under the Jollibee name
When McDonald's entered the Philippines, friends advised the family to sell or close, and they stayed

research_notes: Start date: Rappler (Tony's 2013 speech), WIPO and Ernesto Tanmantiong's 2023 speech all put the first parlours in 1975, and all sources say Tony was 22 at the start (he was born in 1953); Gulf News (2024) says the Magnolia franchise and both branches began in 1978 and were shut 'that same year'. The story uses 1975 for the parlours and 1978 for the switch to Jollibee, the year WIPO and Ernesto both give for the new brand. Locations: Rappler says both parlours were in Cubao; Gulf News says Cubao and Quiapo; the story says only that one was in Cubao. Store count when McDonald's arrived: Tony, in 2013, said Jollibee had 5 stores when friends told him to sell out; Ernesto, in 2023, said 12 stores at McDonald's entry in 1981. The story gives both and who said each. Tony's speech dates the McDonald's moment only as 'just as Jollibee started growing', while Ernesto gives 1981, which is used. The current scale of the group (Ernesto's 18 brands and over 6,600 stores in 34 countries; Gulf News's figures) is not used. The family members named as setting up the first parlours come from Ernesto's speech; the slate names only Tony. Jollibee's own website milestones need JavaScript and the archived copy of its 2012 annual report downloaded damaged, so neither is cited. Seneca's advice concerns personal temper and fortune, applied by analogy to a business plan.
